compatibility_rule: Components exchange `hello` frames listing supported protocol versions as MAJOR.MINOR strings. A peer accepts a message only if its MAJOR equals a supported MAJOR and its MINOR is less than or equal to the highest supported MINOR for that MAJOR. Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored. Incompatible peers receive error code PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE with both version lists so the UI can tell the customer which component to update.

rules.terminal_result: Every command the controller sends is terminated by exactly one `result` frame per command_id (origin `agent` or `relay`). `error` frames are only used when no command_id is known (malformed frame, protocol error, subscription errors). Relay-side rejections before forwarding (signature, ownership, grant, rate limit, PC offline, queue full) are `result{origin:'relay', state:'failed', error}`; an agent connection lost after forwarding yields `result{origin:'relay', state:'outcome_unknown'}` when the agent had acknowledged `executing`, otherwise `result{origin:'relay', state:'failed', error:PC_OFFLINE}`.
rules.duplicate_command: An identical re-submission (same command_id, same signed payload bytes) is answered by re-emitting the previous `result` (or the current ack while still running). The same command_id with different payload bytes is rejected with COMMAND_ID_REUSED.
rules.command_window_and_confirmation: The command's issued_at/expires_at window is checked once when the PC receives the command. Once the PC has emitted confirmation_required, the challenge's expires_at governs: the signed confirmation is accepted iff the challenge is unexpired and unconsumed, and the command then proceeds regardless of its own expires_at. Controllers default disruptive commands to default_confirmed_command_lifetime_seconds so the two windows do not cross by accident.
rules.grants_snapshot: The PC's locally approved controller store (written only at local pairing approval) is the sole source of controller public keys. grants_snapshot is a revocation/intersection list: a kid is usable only if it is locally approved AND present in the latest snapshot; effective capabilities = local ∩ snapshot. A snapshot can never add a controller or widen a grant.
rules.challenge_text: A confirmation challenge travels as an opaque string (challenge_text). The PC stores the exact string it emitted; the relay validates it by strict-parsing a copy and forwards the original string verbatim; the controller strict-parses it once for display and hashes the string verbatim into challenge_digest.
rules.pairing_secret: The PC generates the pairing code locally. The backend only ever receives SHA-256 of the code as a lookup handle; the phone transfers the code out of band (QR or typing) and both devices derive the 6-digit verification code with HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the code, so a backend that substitutes a controller key cannot make the two displays agree.
rules.controller_socket_identity: A controller hello MUST carry kid. The relay binds the socket to (session account, kid) → controller row; hello_ack.controller_id reports it. subscribe/command/confirmation/cancel require a bound, non-revoked controller; every envelope's kid must equal the socket's kid (else UNKNOWN_KEY and close 4003). Revocation sends `revoked` to all sockets bound to that controller and closes them.
rules.state_cache: The relay keeps the last `state` frame per online PC and re-sends it (unchanged) after pc_status on every accepted subscribe. The agent sends a `state` frame immediately after applying grants_snapshot and then on change (debounced 500 ms) and every 30 s.
rules.in_flight: In-flight commands per PC = rows in created|accepted|executing|awaiting_confirmation. The relay gives each forwarded command a hard deadline = max(expires_at, received_at + timeout_ms) + (confirmation_challenge_lifetime_seconds if confirmation==challenge) + 10 s; at the deadline it emits result{origin:relay, state:outcome_unknown} if an executing ack was seen, else result{origin:relay, state:failed, error:COMMAND_EXPIRED}, and frees the slot. Armed power countdowns are exempt until fires_at + timeout_ms.
rules.late_results: After the relay closed a command as outcome_unknown, the agent's journaled result (re-sent on reconnect for commands finished after its last acknowledged frame) MAY be forwarded once as a correction result{origin:agent}; the controller treats it as replacing the prior outcome. Any other post-terminal result is dropped and logged.
rules.mismatch_handling: A command whose account_id/target_pc_id do not match the agent's stored identity is answered result{origin:agent, failed, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH|TARGET_PC_MISMATCH}, is NOT journaled, is logged as a local security event; three within 60 s make the agent close the socket and reconnect with backoff.
rules.agent_identity: The agent's pc_id/account_id are fixed at link time. If hello_ack.pc_id or grants_snapshot.pc_id/account_id differ, the agent closes the socket, stops reconnecting and shows a local re-link prompt. A command received before the connection's first grants_snapshot is answered result{failed, PC_RECONNECTING} and not journaled.
rules.plan_state: pc_enabled=false or controller status=plan_disabled in grants_snapshot are plan/account states, never revocations: local grants stay, the relay refuses routing (PC_PLAN_DISABLED / CONTROLLER_PLAN_DISABLED) and the agent refuses independently.
rules.token_and_entitlement_refresh: PC access tokens are validated only at WebSocket upgrade; an open socket is never closed for token expiry; the agent fetches a new token before reconnecting whenever less than 5 minutes remain. Entitlement assertions follow schemas/entitlement.schema.json: refreshed on connect and at 80% of lifetime; grace only on network error/5xx.
rules.pairing_offline: A claim against an offline PC is accepted (202, state claimed); the relay delivers pairing_request on the agent's next connect (after grants_snapshot) for every unexpired claimed session; the phone polls GET /v1/pairing/{pairing_id}. Pairing session, request and code share one expires_at.
rules.coalescing: Coalescing group = (coalesce key, canonical target JSON or '' when null) per PC across all controllers. The superseded command terminates as result{state:canceled, error:COMMAND_SUPERSEDED, result omitted} and is journaled as such.
